sents: In 2016, the British professional tennis player Andy Murray was ranked as the world's number one.

It was an incredible achievement by any standard – made even more remarkable by the fact that he did this during a period considered to be one of the strongest in the sport's history, competing against the likes of Rafael Nadal, Roger Federer and Novak Djokovic, to name just a few.
Yet five years previously, he had been regarded as a talented outsider who entered but never won the major tournaments.

sents: Of the changes that account for this transformation, one was visible and widely publicised: in 2011, Murray invited former number one player Ivan Lendl onto his coaching team – a valuable addition that had a visible impact on the player's playing style.
Another change was so subtle as to pass more or less unnoticed.
Like many players, Murray has long preferred a racket that consists of two types of string: one for the mains (verticals) and another for the crosses (horizontals).
While he continued to use natural string in the crosses, in 2012 he switched to a synthetic string for the mains.
A small change, perhaps, but its importance should not be underestimated.

sents: The modification that Murray made is just one of a number of options available to players looking to tweak their rackets in order to improve their games.
'Touring professionals have their rackets customised to their specific needs,' says Colin Triplow, a UK-based professional racket stringer.
'It's a highly important part of performance maximisation.'
Consequently, the specific rackets used by the world's elite are not actually readily available to the public; rather, each racket is individually made to suit the player who uses it.
Take the US professional tennis players Mike and Bob Bryan, for example: 'We're very particular with our racket specifications,' they say.
'All our rackets are sent from our manufacturer to Tampa, Florida, where our frames go through a . . . thorough customisation process.'
They explain how they have adjusted not only racket length, but even experimented with different kinds of paint.
The rackets they use now weigh more than the average model and also have a denser string pattern (i.e. more crosses and mains).

sents: Racket modifications mainly date back to the 1970s, when the amateur German tennis player Werner Fischer started playing with the so-called spaghetti-strung racket.
It created a string bed that generated so much topspin that it was quickly banned by the International Tennis Federation.
However, within a decade or two, racket modification became a regularity.
Today it is, in many ways, an aspect of the game that is equal in significance to nutrition or training.

groups.instr: Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?

items.q: People had expected Andy Murray to become the world's top tennis player for at least five years before 2016.
items.exp:
*Bước 1:* mắt thông tin: (a) **người ta kỳ vọng** Murray lên số 1, (b) kỳ vọng đó kéo dài ≥ 5 năm trước 2016.
*Bước 2:* `Andy Murray`, `2016`, `five years` → đoạn 1.
*Bước 3 – Simplify:*
> Murray was ranked number one in 2016. **Yet five years previously, he had been regarded as a talented outsider who entered but never won the major tournaments.**

*Bước 4:*

| Câu hỏi | Bài đọc |
|---|---|
| had expected … to become the top player | (không ai kỳ vọng) |
| for at least five years before 2016 | `five years previously` = 5 năm trước 2016 |
| — | `talented outsider`, `never won` = người ngoài cuộc, chưa từng thắng |

→ **Đáp án: FALSE** (5 năm trước, anh chỉ là "talented outsider", không phải ứng viên số 1)

💡 `Yet` đảo chiều: số 1 năm 2016 ↔ chỉ là người ngoài cuộc 5 năm trước. **`outsider`** = người không được đánh giá cao.

items.q: The change that Andy Murray made to his rackets attracted a lot of attention.
items.exp:
*Bước 1:* `the change … to his rackets` + `attracted a lot of attention`.
*Bước 2:* đoạn 2.
*Bước 3 – Simplify:*
> One change (Lendl) was visible and widely publicised. **Another change was so subtle as to pass more or less unnoticed.** … in 2012 he switched to a synthetic string for the mains.

*Bước 4:* thay đổi **vợt** (dây synthetic) = `so subtle as to pass more or less unnoticed` ↔ `attracted a lot of attention` → **trái ngược**.

→ **Đáp án: FALSE**

💡 **`so + adj + as to V`** = đến mức. **`unnoticed`** ↔ `attracted attention` (trái nghĩa).

⚠️ Thay đổi **được công bố rộng rãi** là việc mời **Lendl** vào đội huấn luyện, **không phải** thay đổi vợt.
pairs: so subtle as to pass more or less unnoticed

items.q: Most of the world's top players take a professional racket stringer on tour with them.
items.exp:
*Bước 1:* mắt thông tin: **hầu hết** top players, **mang theo** stringer **trong tour**.
*Bước 2:* `stringer` → đoạn 3.
*Bước 3 – Simplify:*
> `Colin Triplow, a UK-based professional racket stringer`, says: touring professionals have their rackets **customised to their needs**.

*Bước 4:* bài chỉ nói vợt của tay vợt **được tùy chỉnh**; Triplow chỉ là **người được trích dẫn**. Không nói tay vợt mang stringer theo.

→ **Đáp án: NOT GIVEN**

⚠️ Chữ `stringer` có trong bài nhưng là **nhân vật được trích dẫn**; mắt thông tin "mang theo, đi tour" **không có**.

items.q: Mike and Bob Bryan use rackets that are light in comparison to the majority of rackets.
items.exp:
*Bước 2:* `Mike and Bob Bryan` → đoạn 3.
*Bước 3 – Simplify:*
> The rackets they use now **weigh more than the average model** and also have a denser string pattern.

*Bước 4:* `light in comparison to the majority` ↔ `weigh more than the average` → **ngược**.

→ **Đáp án: FALSE**

💡 `weigh more than the average model` = `heavier than most`. Bài đã **trả lời** câu hỏi (nặng hơn) nên là FALSE, không phải NG.
pairs: light in comparison to the majority
weigh more than the average model

items.q: Werner Fischer played with a spaghetti-strung racket that he designed himself.
items.exp:
*Bước 1:* mắt: Fischer chơi vợt spaghetti (✓?) + **tự thiết kế** (?).
*Bước 2:* `Werner Fischer` → đoạn 5.
*Bước 3 – Simplify:*
> ~~Racket modifications mainly date back to the 1970s, when~~ the amateur German player Werner Fischer **started playing with the so-called spaghetti-strung racket**.

*Bước 4:* mắt 1 có; mắt `designed himself` **không có** (bài không nói ai tạo ra vợt).

→ **Đáp án: NOT GIVEN**

⚠️ `so-called` nghĩa là "được gọi như vậy", **không** nói Fischer là người sáng tạo.

items.q: The weather can affect how professional players adjust the strings on their rackets.
items.exp:
*Bước 2:* `strings` + `adjust` → đoạn 6.
*Bước 3 – Simplify:*
> nearly all professional players experiment with the choice of strings and the tension. **They will continually change it depending on various factors including the court surface, climatic conditions, and game styles.**

*Bước 4:* `weather` = `climatic conditions`; `adjust` = `change`.

→ **Đáp án: TRUE**

💡 **Weather = climatic conditions** (cụ thể → học thuật). `depending on` = chịu ảnh hưởng của.

items.q: It was believed that the change Pete Sampras made to his rackets contributed to his strong serve.
items.exp:
*Bước 2:* `Pete Sampras` → đoạn 9.
*Bước 3 – Simplify:*
> **much of the serving power of Sampras was attributed to the addition of four to five lead weights onto his rackets.**

*Bước 4:*

| Câu hỏi | Bài đọc |
|---|---|
| it was believed | `was attributed to` |
| the change … contributed to | `the addition of … weights` |
| strong serve | `serving power` |

→ **Đáp án: TRUE**

💡 **`be attributed to N`** = được cho là do N. Đây là cách viết "người ta tin rằng" mà không cần chữ `believed`.

groups.instr: Complete the notes below. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

items.q: Mike and Bob Bryan made changes to the types of ……… used on their racket frames.
items.exp:
*Bước 1:* sau `types of`, trước `used on…frames` → **danh từ** (vật liệu đưa lên khung vợt).
*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 3):*
> They explain how they have adjusted **not only racket length, but even experimented with different kinds of paint.**

*Bước 4:* `types of` = `different kinds of`; `experimented with` ↔ `made changes`.

→ **Đáp án: paint**

💡 **`not only A but even B`**: B là điều gây ngạc nhiên. **`types of = kinds of`**.

items.q: Players were not allowed to use the spaghetti-strung racket because of the amount of ……… it created.
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 5):*
> It created a string bed that **generated so much topspin that it was quickly banned**.

*Bước 4:* `not allowed` = `banned`; `the amount of ___ it created` = `so much ___ generated`.

→ **Đáp án: topspin**

💡 **`so much N that…`** (kết quả) ↔ `because of the amount of N`. Đây là **chuyển cấu trúc quả → nhân**.

items.q: Changes to rackets can be regarded as being as important as players' diets or the ……… they do.
items.exp:
*Bước 1:* sau `the`, trước `they do` → **danh từ** (thứ người chơi **làm**).
*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 5):*
> Today it is **an aspect of the game that is equal in significance to nutrition or training.**

*Bước 4:* `players' diets` = `nutrition`; `as important as` = `equal in significance to`.

→ **Đáp án: training**

💡 **`equal in significance to`** = `as important as`: cụm **danh từ hóa** của so sánh bằng. `training` (danh từ không đếm được) đi với `do`.

items.q: All rackets used to have natural strings made from the ……… of animals.
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 7):*
> At one time, all rackets were strung with **natural gut made from the outer layer of sheep or cow intestines.**

*Bước 4:* `animals` = `sheep or cow`; `made from the ___` = `made from … intestines`.

→ **Đáp án: intestines** (chấp nhận `gut` theo sách)

⚠️ `outer layer` là bẫy nhỏ: chỗ trống là **bộ phận cơ thể** (intestines), không phải "layer".

items.q: Pete Sampras had metal ……… put into the frames of his rackets.
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 9):*
> the addition of **four to five lead weights** onto his rackets.

*Bước 4:* `metal` = `lead` (cụ thể → khái quát); `put into` = `addition of`.

→ **Đáp án: weights**

💡 **Specific → general:** `lead` → `metal`. Đáp án là danh từ **số nhiều** đúng như bài.

items.q: Gonçalo Oliveira changed the ……… on his racket handles.
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 10):*
> Oliveira **replaced the original grips of his rackets** with something thinner.

*Bước 4:* `changed` = `replaced`.

→ **Đáp án: grips**

paras.label: A
sents: When one mentions pirates, an image springs to most people's minds of a crew of misfits, daredevils and adventurers in command of a tall sailing ship in the Caribbean Sea.

Yet from the first to the third millennium BCE, thousands of years before these swashbucklers began spreading fear across the Caribbean, pirates prowled the Mediterranean, raiding merchant ships and threatening vital trade routes.
However, despite all efforts and the might of various ancient states, piracy could not be stopped.
The situation remained unchanged for thousands of years.
Only when the pirates directly threatened the interests of ancient Rome did the Roman Republic organise a massive fleet to eliminate piracy.
Under the command of the Roman general Pompey, Rome eradicated piracy, transforming the Mediterranean into 'Mare Nostrum' (Our Sea).

paras.label: B
sents: Although piracy in the Mediterranean is first recorded in ancient Egypt during the reign of Pharaoh Amenhotep III (c 1390–1353 BCE), it is reasonable to assume it predated this powerful civilisation.
This is partly due to the great importance the Mediterranean held at this time, and partly due to its geography.
While the Mediterranean region is predominantly fertile, some parts are rugged and hilly, even mountainous.
In the ancient times, the inhabitants of these areas relied heavily on marine resources, including fish and salt.
Most had their own boats, possessed good seafaring skills, and unsurpassed knowledge of the local coastline and sailing routes.
Thus, it is not surprising that during hardships, these men turned to piracy.
Geography itself further benefited the pirates, with the numerous coves along the coast providing places for them to hide their boats and strike undetected.
Before the invention of ocean-going caravels* in the 15th century, ships could not easily cross long distances over open water.
Thus, in the ancient world most were restricted to a few well-known navigable routes that followed the coastline.
Caught in a trap, a slow merchant ship laden with goods had no other option but to surrender.
In addition, knowledge of the local area helped the pirates to avoid retaliation once a state fleet arrived.

A pirate fleet would serve in the first wave of attack, preparing the way for the navy.
Some of the regions were known for providing safe harbours to pirates, who, in return, boosted the local economy.

paras.label: D
sents: The first known record of a named group of Mediterranean pirates, made during the rule of ancient Egyptian Pharaoh Akhenaten (c 1353–1336 BCE), was in the Amarna Letters.
These were extracts of diplomatic correspondence between the pharaoh and his allies, and covered many pressing issues, including piracy.
It seems the pharaoh was troubled by two distinct pirate groups, the Lukka and the Sherden.
Despite the Egyptian fleet's best efforts, the pirates continued to cause substantial disruption to regional commerce.
In the letters, the king of Alashiya (modern Cyprus) rejected Akhenaten's claims of a connection with the Lukka (based in modern-day Turkey).
The king assured Akhenaten he was prepared to punish any of his subjects involved in piracy.

paras.label: E
sents: The ancient Greek world's experience of piracy was different from that of Egyptian rulers.
While Egypt's power was land-based, the ancient Greeks relied on the Mediterranean in almost all aspects of life, from trade to warfare.
Interestingly, in his works the Iliad and the Odyssey, the ancient Greek writer Homer not only condones, but praises the lifestyle and actions of pirates.
The opinion remained unchanged in the following centuries.
The ancient Greek historian Thucydides, for instance, glorified pirates' daring attacks on ships or even cities.
For Greeks, piracy was a part of everyday life.
Even high-ranking members of the state were not beyond engaging in such activities.

According to the Greek orator Demosthenes, in 355 BCE, Athenian ambassadors made a detour from their official travel to capture a ship sailing from Egypt, taking the wealth found onboard for themselves!
The Greeks' liberal approach towards piracy does not mean they always tolerated it, but attempts to curtail piracy were hampered by the large number of pirates operating in the Mediterranean.

paras.label: F
sents: The rising power of ancient Rome required the Roman Republic to deal with piracy in the Mediterranean.
While piracy was a serious issue for the Republic, Rome profited greatly from its existence.
Pirate raids provided a steady source of slaves, essential for Rome's agriculture and mining industries.
But this arrangement could work only while the pirates left Roman interests alone.
Pirate attacks on grain ships, which were essential to Roman citizens, led to angry voices in the Senate, demanding punishment of the culprits.
Rome, however, did nothing, further encouraging piracy.
By the 1st century BCE, emboldened pirates kidnapped prominent Roman dignitaries, asking for a large ransom to be paid.
Their most famous hostage was none other than Julius Caesar, captured in 75 BCE.

The time had come for concerted action.

passages.title: The persistence and peril of misinformation

sents: Misinformation – both deliberately promoted and accidentally shared – is perhaps an inevitable part of the world in which we live, but it is not a new problem.
People likely have lied to one another for roughly as long as verbal communication has existed.
Deceiving others can offer an apparent opportunity to gain strategic advantage, to motivate others to action, or even to protect interpersonal bonds.
Moreover, people inadvertently have been sharing inaccurate information with one another for thousands of years.

simp.note: Bỏ – both deliberately… –. but đảo chiều

simp.text: People have lied for as long as verbal communication has existed
simp.note: Bỏ likely, roughly

simp.text: Deceiving others can offer an opportunity to gain advantage, motivate others, or protect bonds
simp.note: Giữ các lý do cố ý (Q27 D)

- ① không phải vấn đề mới → ② bằng chứng: nói dối lâu đời → ③ vì sao nói dối (nhiều lợi ích) → ④ **Moreover**: lan truyền vô ý cũng lâu đời.
- Hai nhánh: **cố ý** (②③) và **vô ý** (④).
paras.main: Thông tin sai không phải vấn đề mới và lan truyền vì nhiều lý do, cố ý lẫn vô ý.

sents: However, we currently live in an era in which technology enables information to reach large audiences distributed across the globe, and thus the potential for immediate and widespread effects from misinformation now looms larger than in the past.
Yet the means to correct misinformation might, over time, be found in those same patterns of mass communication and of the facilitated spread of information.

simp.note: Bỏ distributed across the globe, immediate and widespread

simp.text: Yet the means to correct misinformation might be found in those same patterns of mass communication
simp.note: Giữ (Q28 A). Yet đảo chiều

paras.conn:
- ① công nghệ làm tác hại lớn hơn → ② **Yet**: nhưng cũng chính nó có thể giúp sửa.
- `those same patterns` (②) = công nghệ truyền thông đại chúng ở ①.
paras.main: Công nghệ khiến thông tin sai lan rộng hơn, nhưng cũng có thể là công cụ để sửa chữa.

sents: The main worry regarding misinformation is its potential to unduly influence attitudes and behavior, leading people to think and act differently than they would if they were correctly informed, as suggested by the research teams of Stephan Lewandowsky of the University of Bristol and Elizabeth Marsh of Duke University, among others.

In other words, we worry that misinformation might lead people to hold misperceptions (or false beliefs) and that these misperceptions, especially when they occur among large groups of people, may have detrimental, downstream consequences for health, social harmony, and the political climate.

simp.note: Bỏ leading people to… (V-ing), as suggested by the research teams of… among others (nguồn)

simp.note: Bỏ In other words, (or false beliefs), especially when…, liệt kê health, social harmony…

- ① nỗi lo chính: ảnh hưởng thái độ, hành vi → ② `In other words`: nói lại rõ hơn: sinh ra nhận thức sai → hậu quả có hại.
- `In other words` báo hiệu ② **diễn đạt lại** ①.
paras.main: Mối lo chính là thông tin sai làm người ta nhận thức sai và gây hậu quả xấu cho sức khỏe, xã hội, chính trị.

sents: At least three observations related to misinformation in the contemporary mass-media environment warrant the attention of researchers, policy makers, and really everyone who watches television, listens to the radio, or reads information online.
First of all, people who encounter misinformation tend to believe it, at least initially.
Secondly, electronic and print media often do not block many types of misinformation before it appears in content available to large audiences.
Thirdly, countering misinformation once it has enjoyed wide exposure can be a resource-intensive effort.

simp.text: media often do not block misinformation before it appears

paras.conn:
- ① nêu "ba quan sát" → ②③④ **First of all / Secondly / Thirdly**: triển khai từng quan sát.
- Cấu trúc **liệt kê có số**: đoạn 5, 6, 7 sẽ phát triển lần lượt ba ý này.
paras.main: Có ba vấn đề đáng chú ý: người ta dễ tin thông tin sai, truyền thông không chặn trước, và sửa sai sau tốn nhiều nguồn lực.

sents: Knowing what happens when people initially encounter misinformation holds tremendous importance for estimating the potential for subsequent problems.

Although it is fairly routine for individuals to come across information that is false, the question of exactly how – and when – we mentally label information as true or false has garnered philosophical debate.

The dilemma is neatly summarized by a contrast between how the 17th-century philosophers René Descartes and Baruch Spinoza described human information engagement, with conflicting predictions that only recently have been empirically tested in robust ways.

Descartes argued that a person only accepts or rejects information after considering its truth or falsehood; Spinoza argued that people accept all encountered information (or misinformation) by default and then subsequently verify or reject it through a separate cognitive process.

In recent decades, empirical evidence from the research teams of Erik Asp of the University of Chicago and Daniel Gilbert at Harvard University, among others, has supported Spinoza's account: people appear to encode all new information as if it were true, even if only momentarily, and later tag the information as being either true or false, a pattern that seems consistent with the observation that mental resources for skepticism physically reside in a different part of the brain than the resources used in perceiving and encoding.

simp.note: Bỏ for estimating the potential for subsequent problems

simp.text: Although , how and when we label it true or false has garnered debate
simp.note: Giữ vế routine cho Q31

simp.text: The dilemma is summarized by a contrast between Descartes and Spinoza, with conflicting predictions
simp.note: Giữ conflicting predictions (Q32). Bỏ 17th-century, that only recently have been tested…

simp.text: Descartes: accept/reject after considering truth; Spinoza: accept all by default, then verify through a separate cognitive process
simp.note: Giữ (Q33). Dấu ; chia hai quan điểm

simp.text: evidence has supported Spinoza: people encode all information as if true, even if only momentarily, and later tag it true or false; skepticism resources reside in a different part of the brain
simp.note: Giữ (Q34, Q35, Q36). Bỏ nguồn Erik Asp… Gilbert…

paras.conn:
- ① tầm quan trọng → ② cái ai cũng biết (tiếp xúc thường xuyên) + câu hỏi còn tranh cãi → ③ **hai triết gia** đối lập → ④ nội dung hai quan điểm → ⑤ bằng chứng mới ủng hộ **Spinoza**.
- Chuỗi: **vấn đề → tranh luận → hai phe → bằng chứng nghiêng về một phe**.
paras.main: Có hai quan điểm trái ngược về cách ta xử lý thông tin; bằng chứng hiện nay ủng hộ Spinoza: ta chấp nhận mọi thứ trước, kiểm chứng sau.

sents: What about our second observation that misinformation often can appear in electronic or print media without being preemptively blocked?
In support of this, one might consider the nature of regulatory structures in the United States: regulatory agencies here tend to focus on post hoc detection of broadcast information.
Organizations such as the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) offer considerable monitoring and notification functions, but these roles typically do not involve preemptive censoring.

The FDA oversees direct-to-consumer prescription drug advertising, for example, and has developed mechanisms such as the 'Bad Ad' program, through which people can report advertising in apparent violation of FDA guidelines on drug risks.
Such programs, although laudable and useful, do not keep false advertising off the airwaves.
In addition, even misinformation that is successfully corrected can continue to affect attitudes.

simp.note: Giữ (Q30 D). Although A, B → B chính

simp.text: In addition, even corrected misinformation can continue to affect attitudes

paras.conn: - ① quan sát 2 → ② quy định Mỹ chỉ phát hiện **sau** → ③④ ví dụ FDA: giám sát, báo cáo, **không** chặn trước → ⑤ kết luận: không ngăn được quảng cáo sai → ⑥ thêm: sửa rồi vẫn còn ảnh hưởng.

sents: This leads us to our third observation: a campaign to correct misinformation, even if rhetorically compelling, requires resources and planning to accomplish necessary reach and frequency.

For corrective campaigns to be persuasive, audiences need to be able to comprehend them, which requires either effort to frame messages in ways that are accessible or effort to educate and sensitize audiences to the possibility of misinformation.
That some audiences might be unaware of the potential for misinformation also suggests the utility of media literacy efforts as early as elementary school.

Even with journalists and scholars pointing to the phenomenon of 'fake news', people do not distinguish between demonstrably false stories and those based in fact when scanning and processing written information.

sents: We live at a time when widespread misinformation is common.
Yet at this time many people also are passionately developing potential solutions and remedies.
The journey forward undoubtedly will be a long and arduous one.

Future remedies will require not only continued theoretical consideration but also the development and maintenance of consistent monitoring tools – and a recognition among fellow members of society that claims which find prominence in the media that are insufficiently based in scientific consensus and social reality should be countered.
Misinformation arises as a result of human fallibility and human information needs.
To overcome the worst effects of the phenomenon, we will need coordinated efforts over time, rather than any singular one-time panacea we could hope to offer.

items.q: Although people have ______ to misinformation, there is debate about precisely how and when we label something as true or untrue.
items.exp:
*Bước 1:* sau `have`, trước `to` → **danh từ + to**: `exposure to`.
*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 5):*
> **it is fairly routine for individuals to come across information that is false.**

*Bước 4:* `fairly routine to come across` = `frequent exposure`.

→ **Đáp án: G (frequent exposure)**

💡 **`have exposure to N`** = tiếp xúc với N. `routine` = `frequent` (thường lệ → thường xuyên).

items.q: The philosophers Descartes and Spinoza had ______ about how people engage with information.
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify:*
> a contrast between how the 17th-century philosophers described human information engagement, **with conflicting predictions.**

*Bước 4:* `conflicting predictions` ↔ `different ideas`.

→ **Đáp án: J (different ideas)**

⚠️ **A (constant conflict)** cũng có chữ `conflict` nhưng **không đủ nghĩa** (không phải "xung đột liên tục"). Câu sau còn mô tả hai quan điểm → **different ideas**.

items.q: Moreover, Spinoza believes that a distinct ______ is involved in these stages.
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify:*
> Spinoza argued that people accept all information by default and then **verify or reject it through a separate cognitive process.**

*Bước 4:* `distinct` = `separate`; `___ involved` = `cognitive process`; `cognitive` = `mental`; `process` = `operation`.

→ **Đáp án: H (mental operation)**

💡 **Học thuật hóa:** `cognitive process` → `mental operation`. Cả hai từ đều được thay bằng từ đồng nghĩa.

items.q: Recent research has provided ______ for Spinoza's theory and it would appear that people accept all encountered information as if it were t …
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify:*
> In recent decades, **empirical evidence** … has supported Spinoza's account.

*Bước 4:* `supported` ↔ `provided ___ for`; `empirical evidence` ↔ `additional evidence`.

→ **Đáp án: B (additional evidence)**

items.q: … ld appear that people accept all encountered information as if it were true, even if this is for an extremely ______ , and do not label the information as true or false until later.
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify:*
> people appear to encode all new information as if it were true, **even if only momentarily.**

*Bước 4:* `momentarily` = `for an extremely short period`.

→ **Đáp án: E (short period)**

items.q: This is consistent with the fact that the resources for scepticism and the resources for perceiving and encoding are in ______ in the brain.
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify:*
> mental resources for skepticism **physically reside in a different part of the brain** than the resources used in perceiving.

*Bước 4:* `in a different part` = `in different locations`.

→ **Đáp án: C (different locations)**

💡 `reside in` = `be located in`. Danh từ số nhiều `locations` hợp với `are in ___`.

groups.instr: Do the following statements agree with the claims of the writer in Reading Passage 3?

items.q: Campaigns designed to correct misinformation will fail to achieve their purpose if people are unable to understand them.
items.exp:
*Bước 2:* `campaigns` → đoạn 7.
*Bước 3 – Simplify:*
> **For corrective campaigns to be persuasive, audiences need to be able to comprehend them.**

*Bước 4:* `to be persuasive` = `achieve their purpose`; `need to be able to comprehend` = đảo thành `fail if unable to understand`.

→ **Đáp án: YES**

💡 **Điều kiện cần → điều kiện phủ định:** "cần A để thành công" = "không có A thì thất bại".

items.q: Attempts to teach elementary school students about misinformation have been opposed.
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 7):*
> some audiences might be unaware … suggests **the utility of media literacy efforts as early as elementary school.**

*Bước 4:* tác giả **đề xuất** dạy ở tiểu học; **không nói** từng có sự phản đối.

→ **Đáp án: NOT GIVEN**

⚠️ `elementary school` có trong bài nhưng mắt `have been opposed` **không có**.

items.q: It may be possible to overcome the problem of misinformation in a relatively short period.
items.exp:
*Bước 3 – Simplify (đoạn 8):*
> The journey forward undoubtedly will be **a long and arduous one.** … we will need **coordinated efforts over time, rather than any singular one-time panacea.**

*Bước 4:* `short period` ↔ `long and arduous`, `over time`.

→ **Đáp án: NO**

💡 **`panacea`** = thuốc chữa bách bệnh. `rather than A, B`: B là điều tác giả ủng hộ.

items.q: The need to keep up with new information is hugely exaggerated in today's world.
items.exp:
*Bước 3:* tìm `keep up with new information` / `exaggerated` → **không có** chỗ nào bàn về việc "cần theo kịp thông tin mới".

→ **Đáp án: NOT GIVEN**

⚠️ Bài nói về **lan truyền thông tin sai**, không đánh giá **nhu cầu cập nhật thông tin**. Chủ đề gần nhưng mắt thông tin khác.

## PHẦN A – Simplify 15 câu (tăng dần độ khó)

**Yêu cầu mỗi câu:** (1) viết **khung cấu trúc**, (2) khoanh `[S]` `[V]`, (3) gạch phần phụ, (4) viết lại câu rút gọn, (5) ghi verb pattern (nếu có).

**Mức 1 – Mệnh đề quan hệ, đồng vị ngữ, V-ing**

**A1.** Yet five years previously, he had been regarded as a talented outsider who entered but never won the major tournaments.

**A2.** 'Touring professionals have their rackets customised to their specific needs,' says Colin Triplow, a UK-based professional racket stringer.

**A3.** The ancient Greek historian Thucydides, for instance, glorified pirates' daring attacks on ships or even cities.

**Mức 2 – Liệt kê và ví dụ**

**A4.** They are made from three materials: nylon (relatively durable and affordable), Kevlar (too stiff to be used alone) or co-polyester (polyester combined with additives that enhance its performance).

**A5.** Take the US professional tennis players Mike and Bob Bryan, for example: they have adjusted not only racket length, but even experimented with different kinds of paint.

**A6.** Pirate raids provided a steady source of slaves, essential for Rome's agriculture and mining industries.

**Mức 3 – Nhượng bộ và đối lập**

**A7.** While he continued to use natural string in the crosses, in 2012 he switched to a synthetic string for the mains.

**A8.** Although it is fairly routine for individuals to come across information that is false, the question of exactly how – and when – we mentally label information as true or false has garnered philosophical debate.

**A9.** Such programs, although laudable and useful, do not keep false advertising off the airwaves.

**Mức 4 – Cấu trúc đặc biệt (Only when, so… as to, rather than)**

**A10.** Only when the pirates directly threatened the interests of ancient Rome did the Roman Republic organise a massive fleet to eliminate piracy.

**A11.** Another change was so subtle as to pass more or less unnoticed.

**A12.** To overcome the worst effects of the phenomenon, we will need coordinated efforts over time, rather than any singular one-time panacea we could hope to offer.

**Mức 5 – Câu rất dài, nhiều tầng**

**A13.** However, we currently live in an era in which technology enables information to reach large audiences distributed across the globe, and thus the potential for immediate and widespread effects from misinformation now looms larger than in the past.

**A14.** Descartes argued that a person only accepts or rejects information after considering its truth or falsehood; Spinoza argued that people accept all encountered information (or misinformation) by default and then subsequently verify or reject it through a separate cognitive process.

**A15.** The main worry regarding misinformation is its potential to unduly influence attitudes and behavior, leading people to think and act differently than they would if they were correctly informed, as suggested by the research teams of Stephan Lewandowsky of the University of Bristol and Elizabeth Marsh of Duke University, among others.

## PHẦN B – Read Connection 4 đoạn

**Yêu cầu mỗi đoạn:** (1) Simplify từng câu, (2) ghi **quan hệ** giữa các câu (`cùng ý` / `đối lập` / `ví dụ` / `nguyên nhân` / `kết quả` / `trình tự`), (3) chỉ ra từ lặp lại hoặc thay thế (`this`, `it`, `these`…), (4) viết **Main idea** một câu.

> 💡 Làm Phần B **trước khi** đọc lại phần phân tích đoạn tương ứng ở trên.

**B1.** *(Passage 1, đoạn 7)*
> At one time, all tennis rackets were strung with natural gut made from the outer layer of sheep or cow intestines. This all changed in the early 1990s with the development of synthetic strings that were cheaper and more durable. They are made from three materials: nylon (relatively durable and affordable), Kevlar (too stiff to be used alone) or co-polyester (polyester combined with additives that enhance its performance). Even so, many professional players continue to use a 'hybrid set-up', where a combination of both synthetic and natural strings are used.

*Câu hỏi thêm:* `This all changed` đảo chiều từ ý gì sang ý gì? `They` ở câu ③ chỉ cái gì? `Even so` đảo chiều với câu nào?

**B2.** *(Passage 2, đoạn F)*
> The rising power of ancient Rome required the Roman Republic to deal with piracy in the Mediterranean. While piracy was a serious issue for the Republic, Rome profited greatly from its existence. Pirate raids provided a steady source of slaves, essential for Rome's agriculture and mining industries. But this arrangement could work only while the pirates left Roman interests alone. Pirate attacks on grain ships, which were essential to Roman citizens, led to angry voices in the Senate, demanding punishment of the culprits. Rome, however, did nothing, further encouraging piracy. By the 1st century BCE, emboldened pirates kidnapped prominent Roman dignitaries, asking for a large ransom to be paid. Their most famous hostage was none other than Julius Caesar, captured in 75 BCE.

*Câu hỏi thêm:* `this arrangement` chỉ cái gì? Chữ nào cho biết "thỏa thuận ngầm" bị phá vỡ? `however` ở câu ⑥ đảo chiều với ý nào?

**B3.** *(Passage 3, đoạn 5, khó)*
> Although it is fairly routine for individuals to come across information that is false, the question of exactly how – and when – we mentally label information as true or false has garnered philosophical debate. The dilemma is neatly summarized by a contrast between how the 17th-century philosophers René Descartes and Baruch Spinoza described human information engagement, with conflicting predictions that only recently have been empirically tested in robust ways. Descartes argued that a person only accepts or rejects information after considering its truth or falsehood; Spinoza argued that people accept all encountered information by default and then subsequently verify or reject it through a separate cognitive process.

*Câu hỏi thêm:* Ý chính của câu ② nằm ở vế trước hay sau `Although`? `The dilemma` chỉ cái gì? Dấu `;` chia câu ④ thành mấy quan điểm?

**B4.** *(Passage 3, đoạn 8)*
> We live at a time when widespread misinformation is common. Yet at this time many people also are passionately developing potential solutions and remedies. The journey forward undoubtedly will be a long and arduous one. Misinformation arises as a result of human fallibility and human information needs. To overcome the worst effects of the phenomenon, we will need coordinated efforts over time, rather than any singular one-time panacea we could hope to offer.

*Câu hỏi thêm:* `Yet` đảo chiều với câu nào? `the phenomenon` chỉ cái gì? Câu nào là kết luận quan trọng nhất?
